title: Subscription State Diagram
purpose: Subscription lifecycle states showing the minimal two-state machine (active → canceled) with no expiry, pause, or renewal mechanisms — subscriptions are permanent one-time crypto payments
description: The subscription state machine has only two states: active (initial state after crypto payment verification grants permanent access to subscriber-only content) and canceled (fan requests cancellation via subscription.service.ts). There is no expired state, no paused state, no billing renewal logic, and no auto-transition. The stripe_subscription_id column is repurposed to store the crypto transaction hash. Subscriptions are one-time payments that grant permanent access until explicitly canceled by the fan.

actors.label: Fan (Subscriber)
actors.description: User who purchased a subscription to a creator

systems.label: Backend API (Express)
systems.description: Subscription service handlers for create, cancel, and tier change

modules.label: Subscription Service
modules.description: Manages subscription lifecycle — createSubscriptionForUser, cancelFanSubscription, changeSubscriptionTier

modules.label: Subscription Model
modules.description: Database access layer for subscriptions table

dataStores.label: Supabase PostgreSQL
dataStores.description: subscriptions table with columns: id, fan_id, creator_id, tier_id, status (active/canceled), stripe_subscription_id (stores txHash), start_date, end_date, next_billing_date

entryPoints.label: Crypto Payment Verified
entryPoints.description: Successful crypto payment verification triggers subscription creation with status active

entryPoints.label: Cancel Request
entryPoints.description: Fan sends DELETE /api/v1/subscriptions/:id to cancel subscription

exitPoints.label: Active Subscription
exitPoints.description: Fan has access to subscriber-only content; permanent until canceled

exitPoints.label: Canceled Subscription
exitPoints.description: Subscription terminated; fan loses subscriber access; terminal state

preconditions: Fan is authenticated with valid JWT
Crypto payment has been verified on-chain (txHash validated)
postconditions: Active: Fan can view subscriber-only content, subscription record has status=active
Canceled: Fan loses access to subscriber-only content, subscription has status=canceled and end_date=now()

nodes.label: [*] Initial
nodes.description: No subscription exists for this fan-creator pair

nodes.label: Active
nodes.description: Fan has paid crypto subscription and has access to subscriber-only content. stripe_subscription_id stores txHash. No expiry — permanent access.

nodes.label: Canceled
nodes.description: Fan requested cancellation. status=active changed to canceled. end_date=now(). Fan loses subscriber-only access. Terminal state.

nodes.label: [*] — Active Exit
nodes.description: Permanent access ends only when fan cancels

nodes.label: [*] — Canceled Exit
nodes.description: Terminal state — cannot reactivate, must re-subscribe

nodes.label: Create Subscription
nodes.description: After crypto payment verification, insert subscription record with status=active, stripe_subscription_id=txHash, start_date=now(), next_billing_date=now()+30days

nodes.label: Cancel Subscription
nodes.description: Fan calls DELETE endpoint; validate subscription ownership and active status; update status=canceled, end_date=now()

nodes.label: Validate Cancel Request
nodes.description: Check subscriptionId is valid integer, fan_id matches owner, status is active

nodes.label: Cancel Validation Failed
nodes.description: Return 400 (invalid ID) or 404 (not found or not owner) or 400 (not active)

nodes.label: Change Subscription Tier
nodes.description: Fan requests tier change; validate subscription is active and new tier exists; update tier_id

nodes.label: Send Welcome DM
nodes.description: If creator configured welcomeMessage.isActive, send personalized DM via MessageService.sendDirectMessage; failure is non-fatal

errorPaths.trigger: Subscription not found or not owned by fan
errorPaths.recovery: Fan verifies subscription ID and retries
Non-fatal — subscription creation not rolled back

errorPaths.trigger: Invalid tier ID for tier change
errorPaths.recovery: Fan selects valid tier from creator's available tiers
Cannot change tier on canceled subscription

validationRules.rule: fan_id must match req.user.id for modify operations
status must be 'active' to cancel or change tier
subscriptionId must exist in subscriptions table

businessRules.rule: No expiry — subscriptions are permanent one-time crypto payments
No pause mechanism — fan must cancel and re-subscribe
No billing renewal — stripe_subscription_id stores crypto txHash, not Stripe subscription ID
Canceled subscriptions remain in DB with status='canceled' — no hard delete
next_billing_date set to now()+30 days on creation but unused (no renewal logic)

securityConsiderations: Cancel validation hides subscription existence with 404 (not 403) when fan doesn't own it
No re-activation mechanism — canceled subscriptions require new crypto payment
stripe_subscription_id semantic confusion — stores txHash but column name implies Stripe ID
No notification to creator when subscription is canceled
performanceConsiderations: Subscription lifecycle operations are lightweight — single DB queries
Tier change is simple tier_id update — no price recalculation
Welcome DM creation adds latency but is fire-and-forget

annotations.text: No expired state — subscriptions never expire. One-time crypto payment grants permanent access.
No paused state — fans must cancel and re-subscribe to pause/resume.
No billing renewal logic — next_billing_date is set but never checked.
stripe_subscription_id column repurposed to store crypto txHash — semantic column misuse.
Welcome DM send is fire-and-forget — failure does not roll back subscription.
